Blocks.Text: LinkedIn DMA APIs use versioning to provide stable and reliable integrations, even as new features are added. Versioning helps you plan, test, and update your integrations seamlessly, ensuring your applications keep working as the APIs evolve.
Our versioned API releases follow a quarterly release schedule.

LinkedIn continuously improves our products, which means our APIs also evolve. We want our API partners to trust in stable integrations and reliable change schedules, so they can plan and execute more effectively.

Blocks.Section: How your API client should use versioning
SectionPath: How your API client should use versioning
Blocks.Text: HTTP headers are used for clients to indicate which API version implementation they expect. Include a request header with the key “Linkedin-Version” and set the value to the version (format: YYYYMM) to correspond with the documentation version you are referencing. Example: “Linkedin-Version: 202511” would indicate that you are using the version published in the month of November.

Blocks.Section: How your API client should use versioning
SectionPath: How your API client should use versioning

Blocks.Text: In many cases, the URL resource paths your integration uses may not change across versions, but the behavior of the individual API methods can change. New parameters or fields may be available on the response schemas.

The API changes must include the Version Header for the version (release) that needs to be adopted. For the November 2025 Release, the versioned header would be: "LinkedIn-Version": "202511". Each version of the LinkedIn DMA API Program has distinct and comprehensive documentation covering all supported APIs.
Each version includes a changelog that lists all changes from the previous version, indicating which resources have been updated or added. Initially, users have the option on each page in the DMA API documentation page to view:
Versioned content: “DMA {Month} 202X”. The following image is an example of how to select the versioned content in the documentation.
LinkedIn DMA API Program publishes new versions every 3 months.

LinkedIn expects every versioned API call to specify a version; the latest version is not applied by default. It is important to us that customers have the best possible experience with LinkedIn integrations.

LinkedIn reserves the right to release a patch version to any API if required for any critical security, privacy issues, or bug fixes. While the likelihood of these scenarios is minimal, we work closely with partners to minimize the impact of any breaking changes.

Blocks.Section: How do I migrate from an older API version to a later version?
SectionPath: How do I migrate from an older API version to a later version?
Blocks.Text: To migrate your app from an older version to a later version, simply update the older version‘s YYYYMM formatted value in the header to the newer version’s value. For example, here’s how you can migrate from the November 2024 version to the November 2025 version.

Blocks.Text:
Avoiding service disruptions; it is important to upgrade to a newer supported version before the older version is no longer supported.
Utilizing new features that are not accessible in the older version.

Blocks.Section: Which version of the API should I migrate to?
SectionPath: Which version of the API should I migrate to?
Blocks.Text: While you can migrate to any later version of the API, we recommend migrating to the latest version to take advantage of all of our latest features.
